# UK Business Expense Categories (2026/27)

## The Golden Rule

An expense is deductible if it is incurred **wholly and exclusively** for the purposes of the trade. If an expense has a dual purpose (business and personal), it is not deductible unless the personal element is merely incidental, or the business portion can be clearly separated and apportioned.

Source: <https://www.gov.uk/expenses-if-youre-self-employed>

## Fully Deductible Expenses

### Office & Premises
- Rent for business premises
- Business rates
- Utility bills for business premises
- Office supplies and stationery
- Cleaning and maintenance
- Insurance (office, professional indemnity, employers' liability)

### Staff Costs
- Salaries and wages
- Employer National Insurance (15% above £5,000/year secondary threshold)
- Pension contributions (employer)
- Staff training directly related to the role
- Recruitment costs
- Staff welfare and trivial benefits (see below)

### Travel & Subsistence
- Train, bus, and air fares for business travel
- Hotel costs for overnight business trips
- Meals during business travel (reasonable amounts)
- Taxi fares for business purposes
- Parking charges on business trips
- Congestion charges on business journeys

### Mileage (using personal vehicle for business)

HMRC approved mileage rates (unchanged for years):
- **Car or van**: 45p per mile for the first 10,000 business miles, 25p thereafter
- **Motorcycle**: 24p per mile
- **Bicycle**: 20p per mile
- **Passenger payment**: 5p per mile per passenger
- These rates cover fuel, insurance, wear and tear
- Must keep a mileage log: dates, destinations, business purpose
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-travel-mileage-and-fuel-allowances>

### Professional Services
- Accountancy fees
- Legal fees (related to trade, not capital)
- Consultancy fees
- Audit fees
- Professional body memberships (if relevant to the business — see HMRC's approved list)

### Technology & Software
- SaaS subscriptions and cloud services
- Domain names and hosting
- Computer equipment under £1,000 (or use AIA for larger amounts — see Capital Allowances)
- Phone contracts and mobile data
- Internet/broadband for business

### Marketing & Sales
- Advertising (online and offline)
- Website design and development
- PR and communications
- Business cards and promotional materials
- Trade show and exhibition costs

### Financial
- Bank charges and fees
- Credit card charges (business card)
- Interest on business loans
- Foreign exchange losses (trading)
- Bad debts written off (if previously included in turnover)

## Partially Deductible / Special Rules

### Home Office

**Sole traders — simplified expenses**:
- £10/month for 25-50 hours/month of business use
- £18/month for 51-100 hours/month
- £26/month for 101+ hours/month
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/simpler-income-tax-simplified-expenses/working-from-home>

**Sole traders — actual cost method** (alternative):
- Calculate the proportion of home used for business (e.g. 1 room out of 5 = 20%)
- Apply that proportion to mortgage interest, council tax, utilities, insurance
- Adjust for time spent (e.g. 8 hours / 24 hours)
- Be careful with capital gains: exclusive use of a room can affect main residence relief

**Limited companies**:
- The simplified rates do NOT apply to limited companies
- Director can be reimbursed up to £6/week (£312/year) tax-free without supporting calculation
- For higher amounts, must do an actual cost calculation with supporting evidence
- Or formal "rental agreement" between director and company (but this creates personal taxable rental income)

### Telephone
- Business calls: fully deductible
- Mobile contract: deductible if a business contract (single phone per employee can be tax-free)
- Home landline: only the business call element (not the line rental unless a dedicated business line)

### Cars
- Company cars: capital allowances based on CO2 emissions
- Fuel benefit charge if company provides private fuel
- Electric vehicles: 100% first-year allowance, low BIK rate (2% historically — verify current rate at gov.uk)
- For sole traders: usually personal car + mileage claim is more efficient than company car

## Trivial Benefits

Tax-free for employees and directors if **all** these are met:
- Cost is **£50 or less per benefit (inc VAT)**
- Not cash or a cash voucher
- Not a reward for work or in a contract
- Not an annual performance bonus

**Director cap**: directors of close companies are limited to **£300 per tax year** total in trivial benefits (typical example: 6 × £50 gifts).

Source: <https://www.gov.uk/expenses-and-benefits-trivial-benefits>

## NOT Deductible

### Client Entertaining
- Meals, drinks, or events with clients or potential clients: **never deductible** for Corporation Tax
- VAT on client entertaining is also not reclaimable
- Still record these transactions for accounting completeness

### Clothing
- Everyday clothing (even if only worn for work): not deductible
- Uniforms, protective clothing, theatrical costumes: deductible
- The test: would a reasonable person wear it outside work?

### Fines & Penalties
- Parking fines, speeding fines, HMRC penalties: not deductible
- Legal costs of defending criminal proceedings: usually not deductible

### Personal Expenses
- Anything with a personal element that is more than incidental
- Gym memberships (unless provided to all staff as a benefit, with BIK rules)
- Childcare (unless via tax-free childcare or workplace nursery scheme)
- Commuting costs (home to regular workplace)

### Capital Expenditure
- Not directly deductible as an expense
- Instead, claim through capital allowances (AIA, Full Expensing, WDA)
- Examples: machinery, vehicles, major equipment, building works

## Capital Allowances Quick Reference (2026/27)

- **Annual Investment Allowance (AIA)**: £1,000,000/year — 100% first-year deduction on qualifying plant & machinery. Available to sole traders, partnerships, and companies.
- **Full Expensing**: 100% first-year on qualifying main-rate assets. **Companies only**, not sole traders/partnerships.
- **Writing Down Allowance**: 18% (main pool) or 6% (special rate) on a reducing balance.

## Record-Keeping Requirements

- **Limited companies**: keep records for **6 years** from end of accounting period
- **Sole traders**: keep records for **5 years** from 31 January following end of tax year
- Digital copies are acceptable (photo or scan)
- Records must show: date, amount, supplier, what was purchased
- For mileage: date, start/end location, business purpose, miles driven
- For entertainment: who was entertained, business purpose, amount

## Annual Tax-Free Allowances (2026/27)

| Benefit | Annual Limit | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| Trivial benefits (per benefit) | £50 inc VAT | Not cash, not contractual |
| Trivial benefits (director cap) | £300/year total | Close company directors only |
| Annual staff party | £150 per head | Annual events, available to all staff, inclusive of VAT |
| Mobile phone | 1 per employee | Must be a company contract |
| Pension contributions | £60,000 annual allowance | Tapered above £260k income |
| Cycle to Work scheme | No statutory cap | Salary sacrifice, market rate |
| Eye tests | Unlimited | If VDU user |
| Homeworking allowance (Ltd) | £6/week (£312/year) | No receipts needed for this flat rate |
